blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-migration-1 (Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration or backup) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-migration-2 (Account JSON field rename is a breaking API change not marked BREAKING) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
-- Drop the column left from the 2023 import.
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
findings.recommendation: Add `migrations/0005_drop_legacy_email.down.sql` (re-adding `legacy_email TEXT`), as 0004 has a down file, and add a backup step (e.g. copy `id, legacy_email` to an archive table or a dump) before the drop; or state in the plan why the data can be lost and how to recover it.
findings.title: Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration or backup

findings.recommendation: Mark the rename **BREAKING** in the release note with what consumers must do (read `userName` instead of `user_name`), and treat it as a major version bump of the public API.
findings.title: Account JSON field rename is a breaking API change not marked BREAKING

findings.recommendation: Expand then contract — emit both `user_name` (deprecated) and `userName` for at least one release (e.g. a second serialized field or a custom `Serialize`), announce the removal date, then drop `user_name` in a later change.
findings.title: Field removed in the same release as its replacement, no transition period
